previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with worsening dyspnea, productive cough, and subjective fevers. He has multiple myeloma on bortezomib and cyclophosphamide, COPD, and a history of pneumonia. Imaging revealed findings consistent with pneumonia and COPD exacerbation, without evidence of pulmonary embolism or cardiac ischemia. He was treated with levofloxacin, transitioned to moxifloxacin, and received a steroid taper. His symptoms improved, and he was discharged home after three days. A new T8 compression fracture was identified, and he was advised to avoid lifting over five pounds. PCP prophylaxis with Bactrim was initiated due to immunosuppression. Medication adjustments included switching to metoprolol tartrate and tapering prednisone.

Brief Hospital Course:
Mr. ___ is a ___ year old gentleman with a history of multiple 
myeloma s/p Velcade/Cytoxan/Dexamethasone ___, COPD, 
discharged on ___ for pneumonia with albuterol, moxifloxacin x 
10 days, and a prednisone taper, who presented with worsening 
dyspnea, hypoxia, and diffuse wheezing on exam.  

# Hypoxia: 
Patient had been treated by full course of moxifloxacin for 
pneumonia.  Symptoms of shortness of breath began worsening 
towards the end of the prednisone taper. Patient denied any 
chest pain and had no signs or symptoms of heart failure. 
Patient's exam was consistent with COPD exacerbation, though 
there was some concern that symptoms could have been secondary 
to Velcade-induced pneumonitis.  The patient's symptoms did 
appear to respond to steroid treatment.  He was initially given 
IV solumedrol, then transitioned to a prednisone taper starting 
with 60mg.  He was discharged on a 2 week taper of prednisone 
and a total of 7 days antibiotic coverage with a quinolone.  
Prior to discharge, patient's ambulatory O2 saturation was 95% 
on room air.  Patient is not on prednisone at home usually but 
in setting of long-term prednisone and immunosuppression, he was 
re-started on Bactrim DS three days per week for PCP 
___. 

# Multiple Myeloma:  
Patient is s/p Auto-SCT in ___ with disease recurrence in 
___ treated with Velcade/Cytoxan/Dexamethasone in ___.  
SPEP was rechecked for concern of worsening disease, results 
still pending but will be followed up by outpatient hematology 
team. 

# AAA: 
Patient had an abdominal ultrasound to re-evaluate his abdominal 
aortic aneurysm, which appeared to have increased in size since 
previous ultrasound in ___.  A followup appointment was made 
with his vascular surgeon for next week. 
 
# Paroxysmal Atrial Fibrillation: 
Patient appeared to be in normal sinus rhythm for most of this 
hospitalization.  His warfarin has been held in the past month 
while on chemotherapy.  His warfarin was re-started upon 
discharge, 7.5mg MWF and 5mg on other four days of the week.  
___ Healthcare Associates ___ was notified 
that patient is restarting coumadin and will follow his INR.  
INR should be rechecked at patient's followup appointment with 
Dr. ___ on ___.  Patient's outpatient hematology team 
will stop his warfarin prior to another round of chemotherapy.

# Lower Back Pain: 
Patient was continued on outpatient regimen of oxycontin, 
oxycodone, and gabapentin.  
  
# Depression: 
Patient was continued on celexa.

Discharge Instructions:
Dear Mr. ___, 
You were admitted to the hospital because you were having 
difficulty breathing.  It appears that you may have been having 
a flare-up of your emphysema (COPD), though it is possible that 
your lungs had some inflammation from one of your chemotherapy 
drugs.  You had recently been treated for a pneumonia with 
antibiotics, and it seems like your flare-up started a couple of 
days after finishing your antibiotic and steroid treatment.  We 
do not believe you have a new infection.  We have started you on 
more prednisone steroids which you will taper down slowly to 
help decrease the inflammation in your lungs, which seems to be 
helping. We would like you to also take 5 more days of 
antibiotics.

We will also re-start you on your Bactrim 3 days per week to 
help prevent another type of lung infection called Pneumocystis 
that can sometimes happen when your immune system is down.

When you go to Dr. ___ office on ___, ___, please have 
your INR drawn so that the ___ nurses can monitor it 
and call you as appropriate. 

The following changes have been made to your medications: 
- Please START taking prednisone 40mg x 4 more days, then 20mg 
x5 days, then 10mg x6 days
- Please START taking moxifloxacin (antibiotic) 400mg daily x 5 
more days
- Please START taking your warfarin again 7.5mg on ___ 
and 5mg on ___
- Please re-START your Bactrim (TMP/SMX) DS on ___
- Please continue all of your inhalers and medications for your 
emphysema (COPD)

Please be sure to keep all of your followup appointments.
